tags.title: A radio signal, traced to a planet
tags.author: Visual Journalism Desk
tags.description: Astronomers using MeerKAT have localized auroral radio emission to the exoplanet Beta Pictoris b, not its star, and inferred a magnetic field of at least 1,250 gauss. The video explains the evidence, the measurement and its limits, how coverage framed it, and what remains unconfirmed. The study is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed.
tags.keywords: Beta Pictoris b, exoplanet, radio emission, aurora, magnetic field, MeerKAT, electron cyclotron maser, preprint
tags.structure: Question, explanation, evidence, answer; counterpoint and what-we-do-not-know beats
tags.governingMetaphor: Tuning dial with two printed scales: frequency (GHz) and the field it requires (gauss), 2.8 GHz per kilogauss
tags.thesis: MeerKAT radio bursts are the first emission placed on an exoplanet rather than its star, and they set a lower limit of 1,250 gauss on its magnetic field, pending peer review.
tags.houseDeviation: Quote-card opening mark uses indigo instead of signal so that the lower-third signal bar remains the only signal element in quote frames.
tags.disclosure: Synthetic narration. Generated paper and clay illustrations use OpenAI image_gen. ESO and SARAO photographs and the research paper are sourced originals. Original synthesized music and foley.
tags.correctionPolicy: Re-render from this file and append a dated correction note if peer review changes any figure.
